en: The Questions of King Milinda, Chapter on the Determination of Immaterial Phenomena: 1.
The Question on the Arising of Mindfulness
The King said:
"Venerable Nāgasena, in how many ways does mindfulness arise?
"In seventeen ways, Great King, mindfulness arises."
“By what seventeen modes, great king?
“Mindfulness arises, great king, from higher knowledge; mindfulness arises from painful effort;
mindfulness arises from gross consciousness; mindfulness arises from beneficial consciousness; mindfulness arises from harmful consciousness.”
Mindfulness arises from a similar sign; mindfulness arises from a dissimilar sign; mindfulness arises from the recognition of a discourse;
mindfulness arises from a characteristic; mindfulness arises from recollection; mindfulness arises from finger-counting;
mindfulness arises from calculation; mindfulness arises from memorization; mindfulness arises from cultivation.

Mindfulness arises from seeing; mindfulness also arises from hearing, from smelling, from tasting, from touching, and from cognizing. Mindfulness also arises from a book-binding, from a deposit, and from what has been experienced.
How does mindfulness arise from clear comprehension?

Just as, Great King, mindfulness arises for the Venerable Ānanda and the female lay follower Khujjuttarā, or for anyone else who remembers their births through the supernormal knowledge of recollecting past lives—thus mindfulness arises from direct knowledge.
How does mindfulness arise through a reminder?
One who is naturally forgetful is bound by others for the purpose of reminding him; thus mindfulness arises through a reminder.
How does mindfulness arise from gross consciousness?
When one is consecrated in a kingdom, or when one has attained the fruit of stream-entry—thus mindfulness arises from gross consciousness.
How does mindfulness arise from beneficial consciousness?
When one has been comforted by someone, and one remembers, “By such-and-such a person I was comforted in this way,” mindfulness arises from the perception of benefit.
How does mindfulness arise from the perception of harm?
When one has been made to suffer by someone, and one remembers, “By such-and-such a person I was made to suffer in this way,” mindfulness arises from the perception of harm.
How does mindfulness arise from a similar sign?
Having seen a similar person—whether a mother, a father, a brother, or a sister—one recollects them;
or having seen a camel, an ox, or a donkey, one recollects another such camel, ox, or donkey.
Thus mindfulness arises from a similar object.
How does mindfulness arise from a dissimilar object?
One recollects: "Such is the color of so-and-so, such his sound, such his smell, such his taste, such his tangible," and thus mindfulness also arises from a dissimilar object.
How does mindfulness arise from the recognition of speech?
One who is naturally forgetful is reminded by others; through that, he remembers. Thus mindfulness arises from the recognition of speech.
How does mindfulness arise from a characteristic?
When one knows oxen by their natural characteristics or by their marks, mindfulness arises from such marking.
How does mindfulness arise from being reminded?
When one is naturally forgetful, and someone else repeatedly reminds them, saying, "Sir, remember! Sir, remember!", mindfulness arises from being reminded in this way.
How does mindfulness arise from calculation (*muddā*)?
Through training in writing, one knows: "After this syllable, this syllable must be made"; thus mindfulness arises from calculation.
How does mindfulness arise from counting (*gaṇanā*)?
Because they have trained in calculation, calculators can count even much; thus mindfulness arises from calculation.
How does mindfulness arise from retention?
Because they have trained in retention, those who retain can retain even much; thus mindfulness arises from retention.
How does mindfulness arise through cultivation?
Here, a bhikkhu recollects his manifold past abodes, that is to say:
one birth, two births … [and so on] … [as in the standard formula].
Thus one recollects past lives with their modes and details; in this way, mindfulness arises through cultivation.
How does mindfulness arise through the binding of a book?
When kings, failing to remember their instructions, say, "Bring that book," they recollect by means of that book; in this way, mindfulness arises through the binding of a book.
How does mindfulness arise from depositing?
Having seen a deposited object, one remembers it; thus mindfulness arises from depositing.
How does mindfulness arise from what has been experienced?

“Because it has been seen, one remembers a form; because it has been heard, one remembers a sound; because it has been smelled, one remembers an odor; because it has been tasted, one remembers a flavor;
because it has been touched, one remembers a tangible object; because it has been cognized, one remembers a mental phenomenon. Thus, mindfulness arises from what has been experienced.
It is in these seventeen ways, Great King, that mindfulness arises.”
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena!
This concludes the first question on the arising of mindfulness.
